\section[concreto]{concreto — specific, particular}

\label{lesson:ES-C482-concreto}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to foresee, then the Spanish for to watch.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: concreto}
\textbf{concreto} — \textquotedblleft{}specific, particular\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
¿Buscas algo concreto?
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Are you looking for something specific?}
\end{quote}

\emph{En concreto} — specifically.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{concreto} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{concretus}, \textquotedblleft{}grown together, hardened\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), the participle of \emph{concrescere}: \emph{con-} and \emph{crescere}, \textquotedblleft{}to grow\textquotedblright{} — a learned word. Something concrete has set solid.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{concreto}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{concreto}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{concreto}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to foresee, then the Spanish for to watch, then say \emph{concreto} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does concreto mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Specific, particular\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[parecido]{parecido — similar, alike}

\label{lesson:ES-C482-parecido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for to watch, then the Spanish for specific.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: parecido}
\textbf{parecido} — \textquotedblleft{}similar, alike\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Tu bolso es parecido al mío.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Your bag is similar to mine.}
\end{quote}

It goes with \emph{a}: \emph{parecido a}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{parecido} is the participle of \emph{parecer}, \textquotedblleft{}to seem, to look like\textquotedblright{}, from spoken Latin \emph{*parescere}, built on \emph{parere}, \textquotedblleft{}to appear\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short). Things that are \emph{parecidos} look like each other.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parecido}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{parecido}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{parecido}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for to watch, then the Spanish for specific, then say \emph{parecido} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does parecido mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Similar, alike\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[justo]{justo — fair; exactly; tight}

\label{lesson:ES-C482-justo}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for specific, then the Spanish for similar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: justo}
\textbf{justo} — \textquotedblleft{}fair; exactly; tight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
No es justo.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is not fair.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Justo a tiempo} — right on time; \emph{me queda justo} — it is a tight fit.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{justo} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{iustus}, \textquotedblleft{}upright, righteous\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{ius}, \textquotedblleft{}right, law\textquotedblright{}. \textquotedblleft{}Exactly\textquotedblright{} and \textquotedblleft{}tight\textquotedblright{} grew out of \textquotedblleft{}fitting, right\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{justo}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{justo}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{justo}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for specific, then the Spanish for similar, then say \emph{justo} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does justo mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fair; exactly; tight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[rápido]{rápido — fast, quick}

\label{lesson:ES-C482-rapido}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for similar, then the Spanish for fair.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: rápido}
\textbf{rápido} — \textquotedblleft{}fast, quick\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
El tren rápido llega antes.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The fast train gets there sooner.}
\end{quote}

As an adverb it also means quickly: \emph{ven rápido}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{rápido} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{rapidus}, \textquotedblleft{}snatching, swift\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{rapere}, \textquotedblleft{}to snatch\textquotedblright{} — a learned borrowing: the stress stays on the first syllable and the \emph{-p-} is kept.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{rápido}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{rápido}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Spanish for similar, then the Spanish for fair, then say \emph{rápido} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does rápido mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fast, quick\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[la variedad]{la variedad — the variety}

\label{lesson:ES-C482-variedad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Spanish for fair, then the Spanish for fast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: la variedad}
\textbf{la variedad} — \textquotedblleft{}the variety\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Hay mucha variedad de fruta.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There is a wide variety of fruit.}
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{variedad} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{varietas}, \textquotedblleft{}difference, variety\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB 2.1), from \emph{varius}, \textquotedblleft{}different\textquotedblright{}; its ending is the \emph{-dad} of \emph{ciudad}, \textquotedblleft{}city\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for reading notices, forms and messages.
\end{grammarlens}
